claims.claim: Q2 copper production reached 135,900 tonnes, up 25% year over year; QB produced 55,800 tonnes with stable operations for a third consecutive quarter and no TMF-related concentrator downtime.
Copper net cash unit costs fell to US$1.64/lb, supported by higher volumes and by-product credits, while Q2 copper prices averaged US$6.05/lb.

risks: QB tailings-management execution remains operationally material
planned Anglo American merger adds regulatory and integration dependency
contradictions: Current QB stability is materially better than 2025 disruption, but the historical TMF constraint remains relevant until sustained through a longer operating window.
unknowns: durability of QB recovery and throughput improvements
final merger approvals and integration timetable

recommendation.reason: Fresh primary operating evidence establishes a materially changed QB reliability signal and cost profile.
